summary: The great crown of the frozen interior and the western ports: court, iron, harbours, the Northern Accord, Isengard, the old peoples, the silent castle, the far ice and the choice of the Cold Lands in the final war (102 focuses, branches A to J).

ports_against_interior.name: Ports Against the Interior
ports_against_interior.desc: The harbour-masters of the west and the clan-chiefs of the interior have quarrelled for as long as the crown has been worn. The Queen's court spends half its strength keeping the peace between them.

winter_crown_spirit.name: The Winter Crown
winter_crown_spirit.desc: The white banner of Fandanar hangs in every hall of the interior, and the clans have learned to look up when it is raised.

high_crown_of_the_north_spirit.name: High Crown of the North
high_crown_of_the_north_spirit.desc: Crowned twice and owed oaths by a hundred chiefs, the Queen of Coldor speaks and the Cold Lands, for the most part, listen.

chancellors_ledgers_spirit.name: The Steward's Ledgers
chancellors_ledgers_spirit.desc: Every barrel, bale and bar of iron is written in the steward's books. The court may not like the numbers, but it can no longer pretend to ignore them.

ports_ascendant.name: The Ports Ascendant
ports_ascendant.desc: Harbour-masters sit at the Queen's right hand, and her treasury counts its wealth in cogs and cargo. The steadings are told to be patient.

steadings_ascendant.name: The Steadings Ascendant
steadings_ascendant.desc: The clans of the interior are the crown's first care, and their levies are quick to muster. The coast, in the meantime, is left to look after itself.

law_of_the_long_winter_spirit.name: Law of the Long Winter
law_of_the_long_winter_spirit.desc: The law is short and hard and everyone knows it by heart: feed your neighbour, keep your fire and do not sell what the winter will need.

fur_trade.name: The Fur Trade
fur_trade.desc: White-cloaked traders carry the pelts of the north to the western quays. The wealth is real, and the hunters' hunger for coin is real too.

hide_and_wool_spirit.name: Hide and Wool
hide_and_wool_spirit.desc: Felted cloaks, greased boots and good leather mittens are issued to every soldier. The cold has fewer teeth.

long_night_fires.name: Fires Through the Long Night
long_night_fires.desc: The great hearths of the halls never go cold, and builders work by firelight when the sun does not rise.

harbour_charter.name: The Harbour-Master's Charter
harbour_charter.desc: Fair dues, open berths and an honest weigh-house. Captains who put in to a Coldor harbour tend to come back.

cold_seas.name: Masters of the Cold Seas
cold_seas.desc: Cold Coast captains navigate by sounding and instinct through ice and fog that would send a southern crew home in a week.

frozen_crown.name: The Frozen Crown
frozen_crown.desc: A third of the Cold Lands takes counsel from Fandanar, and the Queen finds that hearing many voices keeps her sharp.

one_banner.name: One Banner of the Ice
one_banner.desc: The white banner flies from coast to coast. No chief of the Accord thinks himself a vassal, and none thinks of leaving.

walls_of_isengard_spirit.name: The Walls of Isengard
walls_of_isengard_spirit.desc: The Host breaks itself on Isengard's keeps and grows stronger for it. Every tower taken is a lesson learned and paid for.

cold_lands_at_peace.name: The Cold Lands at Peace
cold_lands_at_peace.desc: The march lies quiet, the passes are open and the Queen's attention is free for the first time in a generation.

yeti_trackers.name: Trackers in the Snow
yeti_trackers.desc: Yeti trackers range ahead of every column and read the drifts as a clerk reads a page. Nobody gets lost, and nobody is ambushed.

giants_on_the_passes_spirit.name: Giants on the Passes
giants_on_the_passes_spirit.desc: A giant on a pass is a landmark, a wall and a rumour all at once. Few raiders test whether the rumour is true.

snow_runners_spirit.name: The Snow-Runners
snow_runners_spirit.desc: Light foot on broad snowshoes cross the drifts in half the time. They arrive tired, and they arrive first.

war_sledges_spirit.name: War-Sledges
war_sledges_spirit.desc: Dog-drawn sledges with shield-wall and bolt-thrower speed across the ice. The supply wagons have no complaint.

white_host.name: The White Host
white_host.desc: Clad in white and drilled in a blizzard, the Host fights as if the cold itself were on its side.

far_ice_wardens.name: Wardens of the Far Ice
far_ice_wardens.desc: A chain of watch-huts across the ice fields keeps travellers alive and strangers noticed.

stand_apart_spirit.name: The Cold Lands Stand Apart
stand_apart_spirit.desc: The Queen has declared that the war in the south is not Coldor's, and the land is quiet. It is a peace paid for with a little pride.

neutral_ports.name: Ports Closed to War
neutral_ports.desc: No ship of war may anchor in a Coldor harbour. Merchants grumble, and the harbours stay empty of trouble.

winter_wall.name: The Winter Wall
winter_wall.desc: Walls of ice and stone close the passes, and ditches are flooded to freeze. Any host that wants the Cold Lands will have to climb for them.

white_companies_abroad.name: The White Companies Abroad
white_companies_abroad.desc: Far from the snow, the volunteers of the Cold Lands fight in white and sing in the old tongue. They are not easy to break.

ports_and_steadings.title: Ports and Steadings
ports_and_steadings.desc: At the long table in Fandanar the Harbour-Master and the Marshal both ask for the Queen's favour. One wants ships to carry the crown's name to the western sea; the other wants levies to hold the passes. Both are right, and only one can be answered first.

options.name: The ports pay for the crown.

fearno_question.title: Fandanar Asks for Friendship
fearno_question.desc: A rider in white furs reaches the stewards of Fearno with a letter under the Queen's seal. Coldor offers the friendship of the Northern Accord and the protection of its spears, and asks only that Fearno name Fandanar its friend.

empty_hall.title: The Empty Hall
empty_hall.desc: The riders from the north say that the light in the silent castle still burns, but nobody comes to the gate any more. The guardian is gone. Fandanar will not ask who ended him.

options.name: Let the north keep its silence.

focuses.name: The Winter Crown of Fandanar
focuses.desc: Queen Vaestia sits beneath the white banner at Fandanar, heir to a crown the interior made in 850 and the ports have never quite forgiven. The first work of a queen is to hear them all.

focuses.name: The Queen's Council
focuses.desc: Vaestia calls her councillors to the long table of Fandanar and asks them for the truth. They give her the whole of it, and she thanks them for it.

focuses.name: The Crown of 850
focuses.desc: In 850 the clans of the interior swore one oath beneath one banner. Isengard remembers the oath too, and remembers refusing it.

effects.tooltip: The interior was made one in 850. Isengard remembers it too.

focuses.name: The Steward's Ledgers
focuses.desc: The Queen's steward lays a year's grain, furs and iron before her in a single book. The books are honest, and the sums are grim.

focuses.name: Ports and Steadings
focuses.desc: The coast wants ships and the hills want levies, and both want the Queen's ear. She must choose whom to disappoint first.

focuses.name: The Marshal's Counsel
focuses.desc: Marshal Grindok Azlen speaks of snow, supply and the hard sums of marching in winter. The council listens, because he has never once been wrong about the cold.

focuses.name: Favour the Ports
focuses.desc: Harbour-Master Alorio's argument carries the day: ships, timber and trade with the West will make Coldor rich, whatever the steadings say.

focuses.name: Favour the Steadings
focuses.desc: The clans of the interior hold the passes and fill the levies. The Queen judges that a crown is only as strong as the steadings that feed it.

focuses.name: One Crown of Ice
focuses.desc: With the quarrel settled, harbour, hill and steading answer to one seat. The Queen's court breathes out.

focuses.name: The Queen's Progress
focuses.desc: Vaestia travels from steading to steading by sledge, eating at every hearth and hearing every grievance. The clans do not forget a ruler who came in person.

focuses.name: Law of the Long Winter
focuses.desc: A law sets out who feeds whom when the snows close the roads. It is written in short, hard sentences, in the manner of the interior.

focuses.name: High Crown of the North
focuses.desc: The Queen is crowned a second time, in the stone hall at the head of the Neck Road. The clans bring white furs and keep their swords.

focuses.name: Iron and Furs
focuses.desc: The wealth of the interior is iron under the rock and fur on the hunters' backs. The Queen resolves to count both and spend them on purpose.

focuses.name: The Deep Iron Mines
focuses.desc: Shafts are sunk below the frost line, braced with timbers hauled from the western slopes. The seams run black and rich.

focuses.name: The Fur Trade
focuses.desc: Traders in white cloaks carry sable, ermine and fox to the western ports, where ship captains pay in silver and spice.

focuses.name: Winter Stores
focuses.desc: Every steading is bidden to lay up grain and salted meat against the long dark, and the Queen's stewards check the barrels one by one.

focuses.name: The Sledge Roads
focuses.desc: Packed-snow roads are marked with cairns and way-houses from the interior to the coast. A laden sledge can cross the Cold Lands before the thaw.

focuses.name: The Forges of Fandanar
focuses.desc: Furnaces roar in the stone halls beneath the Queen's seat. The smiths of Fandanar make blades that do not crack in the cold.

focuses.name: Halls of Stone
focuses.desc: Quarrymen and masons raise long halls where whole clans can winter under one roof. They are warm, and they are built to last.

focuses.name: Hide and Wool
focuses.desc: Fleeces, hides and felted cloth are made in bulk by the steading women. The Host will be clothed before the snow comes.

focuses.name: Fires Through the Long Night
focuses.desc: Great hearths burn in every hall of the Cold Lands from Gaelor to Lumae. Those who tend them are honoured; those who let them die are not.

focuses.name: The Northern Workshops
focuses.desc: In the lee of the mountains, guild halls of smiths, wrights and tanners turn out tools for the whole of the north.

focuses.name: The Western Ports
focuses.desc: Where the Cold Lands meet the western sea, Harbour-Master Alorio keeps a dozen ports open through all but the worst ice.

focuses.name: The Harbour-Master's Charter
focuses.desc: Alorio's charter sets fair dues and open berths for every flag. Captains from the West Lands begin to prefer Coldor's harbours to their own.

focuses.name: Shipwrights of the Cold Coast
focuses.desc: Yards in the fjords build cogs of pine and oak, with hulls tarred against the ice.

focuses.name: Grain from the West
focuses.desc: Traders from the West Lands bring wheat and barley to Coldor's quays in exchange for furs and timber. The winter stores fill without anyone going hungry.

focuses.name: The Windwaith Question
focuses.desc: Windwaith's harbours rival Coldor's on the same coast. The Harbour-Master suggests a compact in place of a quarrel.

focuses.name: Timber for the West
focuses.desc: Western shipyards pay silver for Cold Lands pine. The Queen decides that selling the West its masts is no sin, whatever it builds with them.

focuses.name: The Long Sea Road to Parim
focuses.desc: Cogs of Coldor cross the central sea to the Lake and return with Aenoran silver. It is a long road, and it pays.

focuses.name: The Coastal Watch
focuses.desc: Watch-towers and chain-booms rise at the harbour mouths. Raiders from the sea will find the coast awake.

focuses.name: The Northern Fleet
focuses.desc: Captain Harl of the Cold Coast is given a flotilla of the new cogs and told to keep the sea lanes clear of pirates, and of worse.

focuses.name: Masters of the Cold Seas
focuses.desc: A fleet that sails in ice and fog is a fleet no southern captain wants to meet. The flotillas of the Cold Coast earn a name.

focuses.name: The Northern Accord
focuses.desc: Coldor and Horidor have kept the old league of the north for generations. The Queen sends a rider to Horidor's hall to renew it.

focuses.name: Kinship with Horidor
focuses.desc: Horidor's chief and the Queen share a cup at the border stone. Their clans have married across the line for as long as anyone remembers.

focuses.name: Envoys to the Steadings
focuses.desc: Skilled speakers of the court are sent to the free steadings with gifts of salt and promises of protection.

focuses.name: Highland Roads
focuses.desc: Roads cut across the high passes tie Horidor's valleys to Fandanar. The pack-teams that use them are glad of the way-houses.

focuses.name: Gifts for the Winter Moot
focuses.desc: At the Winter Moot the Queen gives furs, salt and iron to every chief who comes. No one forgets who fed them.

focuses.name: Steading Charters
focuses.desc: Written charters set out what each steading owes and what it is owed. The Queen's seal is cheap to give and dear to break.

focuses.name: Open the Accord
focuses.desc: The Accord's doors are thrown wide. Any steading, town or hold may join, on the Queen's word that it will be protected and not ruled.

focuses.name: The Fearno Question
focuses.desc: Fearno lies between Coldor and the free towns. Its stewards must be asked, with courtesy, whether they will walk the road beside the Accord.

focuses.name: The Coast Towns
focuses.desc: Holdon and Wonderland sell fish and amber from their small harbours. Both would gladly have a strong friend at their backs.

focuses.name: The Frozen Crown
focuses.desc: With a third of the Cold Lands taking her counsel, Vaestia wears her crown among chiefs who have never seen a king.

focuses.name: One Banner of the Ice
focuses.desc: From the western ports to the northern coasts the white banner flies. The Cold Lands have never been so nearly one.

focuses.name: The Isengard Question
focuses.desc: Isengard refused the oath of 850 and has kept its borders with pride ever since. Fandanar must decide whether to answer pride with patience or with iron.

focuses.name: Count Isengard's Forts
focuses.desc: Scouts walk the border and count the towers, ditches and garrisons. The tally is longer than the court expected.

focuses.name: Envoys to Isengard
focuses.desc: The Queen's envoys cross the march under a white flag, with gifts for Isengard's warlord. They are received, though not warmly.

focuses.name: Border Forts of Coldor
focuses.desc: Coldor raises its own line of stone keeps opposite Isengard's towers. Neither side will say they are meant for war.

focuses.name: A Marriage Across the March
focuses.desc: A match is proposed between the house of Fandanar and the house of Isengard. Weddings across the march have ended feuds before.

focuses.name: The Iron Hand
focuses.desc: The Queen resolves that Isengard will be brought to the Accord by force of arms if it will not come by choice.

focuses.name: The Open Hand
focuses.desc: The Queen resolves to offer Isengard a place at the table, with no condition but peace.

focuses.name: The March Forts
focuses.desc: The border keeps are manned and the order given. The war on the march begins, small and bitter, over towers and ford roads.

focuses.name: A Charter for Isengard
focuses.desc: A charter is drawn that lets Isengard keep its warlord, its forts and its law, and asks only that it sit with the Accord.

focuses.name: Isengard Swears
focuses.desc: Isengard's warlord rides to Fandanar and kneels, stiffly, before the Queen. Whatever his pride may be, he has sworn.

focuses.name: Isengard Must Kneel
focuses.desc: Isengard's last refusal ends the Queen's patience. The Winter Host marches, and this time it does not stop at the march.

focuses.name: Kin of the North
focuses.desc: Isengard's hearths are fed from Coldor's stores and its walls mended with Coldor's iron. It is easier to love a friend who feeds you.

focuses.name: The Walls of Isengard
focuses.desc: Isengard's keeps stand on high stone, and the Host must take them one by one. The assault will be long, and cold, and costly.

focuses.name: The Cold Lands at Peace
focuses.desc: The old quarrel is ended, by oath or by conquest. The march falls quiet and the passes stand open from sea to sea.

focuses.name: The Old Peoples of the Ice
focuses.desc: Beyond the last steading live peoples who answer to no crown. The Queen sends gifts instead of orders.

focuses.name: Envoys to the Hunting Grounds
focuses.desc: Messengers carrying salt and iron walk to the yeti of the high hunting grounds. They return with tales, and with a nod.

focuses.name: Envoys to the Frost-King's Hall
focuses.desc: Messengers with gifts climb to the hall of the ice giants of Titanos. The doors are very large, and they open.

focuses.name: Gifts of Salt and Iron
focuses.desc: A second embassy brings what the yeti value: salt for their meat and iron for their tools.

focuses.name: The Giants' Toll
focuses.desc: The giants ask a toll for the passes: so many sacks of grain, so many barrels of mead. It is a price the Queen is glad to pay.

focuses.name: The Old Pacts
focuses.desc: The pacts are sworn with fire and stone. They bind no one to anything but friendship, which is already a great deal.

focuses.name: Trackers in the Snow
focuses.desc: Yeti trackers walk beside the Queen's scouts, and no patrol is lost in the snow while they are near.

focuses.name: Giants on the Passes
focuses.desc: Giants of Titanos stand watch on the high passes, taller than the watchtowers and unimpressed by raiders.

focuses.name: Hearth and Height
focuses.desc: The pacts are renewed at their highest level. In war, the old peoples will answer a call from Fandanar, if they judge it just.

focuses.name: Legends of the Silent Castle
focuses.desc: Traders speak of a castle in the frozen north, and of a light there that does not fail.

effects.tooltip: Traders speak of a castle in the frozen north, and a light that does not fail.

focuses.name: Leave the Hall in Peace
focuses.desc: The Queen decrees that no host of Coldor shall approach the silent castle uninvited. The north is wide enough for both.

focuses.name: The Northern Coast Watch
focuses.desc: Fishing villages on the northern shore are given spyglasses, horns and a signal code. They will see ships long before the ships see them.

focuses.name: Guides of the Snow
focuses.desc: Trappers who know the trails to the far north are paid to guide travellers. They ask no questions, and they remember faces.

focuses.name: Watch-Fires of the North
focuses.desc: Beacons on the northern headlands are lit every night, and a sentry on each counts the ships that pass.

focuses.name: Stand Guard Outside the Hall
focuses.desc: A small company is posted outside the castle gate, to keep strangers away and, if need be, to tell the keeper of the hall that someone is coming.

focuses.name: The Empty Hall
focuses.desc: Word reaches Fandanar that the castle's guardian is gone. What stands in his hall now is a matter for the Queen's council.

focuses.name: A Watch on Mp'E
focuses.desc: With the guardian gone, a company keeps watch on the approaches of the castle, lest the wrong hands claim what lies within.

focuses.name: The Winter Army
focuses.desc: Marshal Grindok Azlen's army drills in the hardest season, because it will have to fight in it.

focuses.name: The Snow-Runners
focuses.desc: Skirmishers on broad wooden snowshoes cross drifts that stop horses. They arrive unseen and leave the same way.

focuses.name: Marshal Grindok's Drill
focuses.desc: The old marshal's drill book is read at every muster: how to march in wind, how to sleep in snow and how to die last.

focuses.name: Wardens of the Peaks
focuses.desc: Mountain wardens trained to hold the high passes are issued the new spears and bows. The passes are theirs.

focuses.name: Frost-Hardened
focuses.desc: Furs, felt and fat-greased boots are issued to every soldier. The cold becomes a nuisance and no longer an enemy.

focuses.name: The Iron Levy
focuses.desc: Each steading sends its quota of men to the Queen's muster, bearing its own spear and shield.

focuses.name: War-Sledges
focuses.desc: Sledges mounted with ballistae and shield-walls speed across the ice behind teams of dogs. They are loud, ugly and very fast.

focuses.name: The Winter Host
focuses.desc: The finest soldiers of the Queen assemble in the great hall of Fandanar, a host that does not fear snow.

focuses.name: The White Host
focuses.desc: Clad in white cloaks and carrying white-painted shields, the army marches out of the blizzard like a second winter.

focuses.name: Beyond the Last Steading
focuses.desc: The Queen's wardens set out for the far north-west, where the maps end and the ice begins. Warden Ysolde leads them.

focuses.name: Wardens of the Far Ice
focuses.desc: A chain of watch-huts is raised across the ice fields, each manned by a warden and a pair of dogs.

focuses.name: The Hunters' Trade
focuses.desc: Walrus-hunters and seal-takers from the far coasts trade tusks and rendered fat for iron and cloth. The Queen's tax-gatherers follow close behind.

focuses.name: The White Road
focuses.desc: A road of packed snow and ice-markers runs from the last steading into the far north-west. It is the first road ever laid there.

focuses.name: Word from the Far Ice
focuses.desc: The wardens report that a man has been found alive in the ice, with no name and no memory of how he came there.

focuses.name: Provisions for the Stranger
focuses.desc: Furs, bread and a guide are sent to the man from the ice to see him south. The Queen asks nothing in return.

focuses.name: The King Without a House
focuses.desc: Travellers from the south say the man from the ice leads a host and is hailed as a king. Fandanar sends greetings, and waits.

focuses.name: The World Beyond the Ice
focuses.desc: War has come to the south, and the Cold Lands cannot pretend not to hear it. The Queen's council meets to choose a road.

focuses.name: The Cold Lands Stand Apart
focuses.desc: Coldor declares that the war in the south is not its war. The ports will close, the passes will be watched and the winter will do the rest.

focuses.name: Timber and Ships for the West
focuses.desc: Coldor sells masts, planking and cogs to the West Lands. The Queen insists on being paid in advance.

focuses.name: The White Companies
focuses.desc: Volunteers from every steading are mustered under white banners to sail south to the living. They go to fight beside strangers, and the Queen blesses them.

focuses.name: Close the Ports to War
focuses.desc: Harbour chains are drawn and the harbour-masters ordered to turn away every ship of war. The merchants complain, and the sea stays quiet.

focuses.name: The Winter Wall
focuses.desc: Walls of ice and stone are thrown across the main passes and coastal approaches. If the war comes north, it will find the Cold Lands ready.

focuses.name: The Cold Endures
focuses.desc: The Cold Lands refused the war and survived it. The Queen's court holds that this, too, is a kind of victory.

focuses.name: The Western Contracts
focuses.desc: Contracts for timber, ships and iron are signed with western shipping houses. The coffers fill and the ports hum.

focuses.name: A Share of the Plunder
focuses.desc: The Western Crossing has begun, and the Queen asks what her share will be. She sends cogs to carry the host of the West.

focuses.name: Answer the Heir's Call
focuses.desc: The King Without a House has come back and asks for the Cold Lands' aid. The White Companies sail.

focuses.name: The White Companies Hold
focuses.desc: Far from home, the White Companies hold a line for the living. They have not been broken, and the Cold Lands sing of them.

focuses.name: The North Remembers
focuses.desc: The war is over, the dark is broken, and the Cold Lands remember who stood at their side. The Queen's court counts its debts and its friends.

focuses.name: Songs of the Long Dark
focuses.desc: The songs the clans sing through the Long Dark tell of a green north, of horse-meadows in the Fandan valley and halls of timber where the ice lies now. The fire-keepers of the Frost-Hall begin to ask the singers where the songs came from.

focuses.name: Ice-Walkers
focuses.desc: In the years when a mild winter lets the ice draw back, the oldest timbers and bronze come out of it on the Frozen Lands. The crown teaches walkers to go and look, with sleds, tents and the sense to turn back in time.

focuses.name: Kin over the Neck
focuses.desc: The clans of the western lands sing of a lost north under a name that sounds very like our own. Envoys go south over the Neck to compare the songs, and to find out whether the clans will hear us as kin.

focuses.name: Kin over the Sea
focuses.desc: The chart-islanders have sea-words older than any chart, and some of them are words for things that only a man of the north would need. A ship goes west to the isles with a fire-keeper and a singer aboard.

focuses.name: The Sun Crown
focuses.desc: The hearth-stone of the old king's hall is in the crown's keeping, and the fire-keepers say that a crown over the ice may also be a crown over the fields that lay beneath it. The free steadings say they will see about that.
